title: Erode Turmeric Crosses Rs 22,000 a Quintal, Highest in Recent Years, as Drought Cuts Arrivals
excerpt: Finger turmeric touched Rs 22,989 a quintal in Erode on Tuesday, its first close above Rs 22,000, after drought shrank cultivation and arrivals fell 25%.
body:
• Finger turmeric at Erode touched Rs 22,989 a quintal on Tuesday, crossing Rs 22,000 for the first time; Monday's maximum was Rs 20,799.
  • The bulb variety rose to Rs 19,699 a quintal, up from Rs 19,011 a day earlier, as the rally spread across grades.
  • Arrivals at Erode have fallen 25% from usual levels as drought cut cultivation and traders stockpile ahead of the February-June season.
  • At Rs 22,989 a quintal, Erode finger turmeric is up about 51% from Rs 15,199 on June 19 — diaspora grocery and spice prices follow Indian mandis with a lag.

Turmeric has set a record in Erode, the Tamil Nadu market that anchors India's trade in the spice. The procurement price of finger turmeric crossed Rs 22,000 a quintal on Tuesday for the first time, reaching Rs 22,989, The New Indian Express reported. A day earlier the same variety's maximum was Rs 20,799 a quintal — a jump of more than Rs 2,000 in a single session. The bulb variety climbed too, from Rs 19,011 to Rs 19,699 a quintal. The last time prices broke a round-number barrier was 2024, when they crossed Rs 21,000.

A Record Built on Drought

Traders and farmers put the rally down to water. Drought conditions prevail across much of the turmeric belt — Erode itself, and the growing regions of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Maharashtra — shrinking both the area planted this year and the crop that was planted. An official of the Horticulture and Plantation Crops department in Erode confirmed cultivation in the district has decreased slightly this year because of drought. S Periyasamy, president of the Lower Bhavani Ayacut Land Owners' Association, said crops on his own farmland have been hit by lack of water.

"This is the first time the procurement price has crossed Rs 22,000."

— M Sathyamurthy, Secretary, Erode Turmeric Merchants' and Godown Owners' Association

Arrivals Down a Quarter as Stockpiling Begins

The new turmeric season normally runs from February to June. With farmers and traders expecting smaller fresh arrivals next season, many have begun stocking turmeric now in anticipation of still higher prices. The result is a squeeze in the spot market: arrivals at Erode have fallen about 25% from usual levels, according to the merchants' association. The same price rise is visible in the other major markets — Nizamabad in Telangana and Sangli in Maharashtra — and on the NCDEX futures exchange, Sathyamurthy said, adding that rainfall in the coming days could swing prices either way.

Most Farmers Sold Before the Spike

Record prices do not mean record incomes for growers. Most farmers in Erode district have already sold their turmeric, Periyasamy said, so the rally mainly rewards the small number of farmers still holding stock — and the traders who built inventories earlier. The run has been steep: finger turmeric stood at Rs 14,000 a quintal on April 20, 2026 and Rs 15,199 on June 19, before this week's record. Periyasamy expects festive-season demand could take prices as high as Rs 30,000 a quintal, though that is his projection, not a market consensus. Broader spice-market reporting also shows firm festival and processing demand across Indian mandis, with export offers steady at firm levels, according to CMB News.

What It Means for Diaspora Kitchens

Turmeric is a daily staple in diaspora kitchens and a wellness-shelf regular in the US, and Erode sets the price tone for the export trade. With Indian mandis at record levels and arrivals down a quarter, imported turmeric powder and whole fingers on US Indian-grocery shelves are likely to get dearer over the coming months rather than cheaper. Households that buy turmeric in bulk for festival cooking may want to stock up before the next round of retail repricing works through.
